title: api & config sketch - model routing + runtime options
content:
Context:
- Quick scratchpad for an internal API shape + runtime config options for model routing & graceful fallback.
- Goal: small, composable config that can be used in Hosted / Dedicated / Private with minimal translation.
- Audience: infra engineers + runtime team for initial implementation (canary first).

Requirements / constraints (high level):
- Support per-request routing policy: prefer-latency | prefer-cost | region-preference | pinned-model-version
- Fallback chains: sequence of compatible model variants (e.g., 70B fp16 -> 70B q4 -> 13B fp16)
- KV/prefix caching hints per-route to optimize warm-starts
- Batching parameters negotiable per route, with global defaults
- Fast failover to lower-tier capacity (gpu pool with lower SLO) + graceful partial responses (if allowed)

Rough API shape (sketch):
- POST /v1/infer
  body: {
    "input": "... prompt ...",
    "route_config": {
      "policy": "prefer-latency",
      "model_preferences": ["redwood/rrhf-70b:2026-02-01", "redwood/rrhf-70b-q4:2026-01-10", "meta/13b-weights:1.2"],
      "region": "us-west1",
      "max_cost_usd": "0.05",
      "kv_cache_hint": { "key": "user-123/prefix-1", "ttl_seconds": 3600 },
      "batching": { "max_tokens": 2048, "max_batch_size": 8, "latency_target_ms": 120 }
    },
    "response_options": { "stream": true, "partial_on_fallback": false, "max_tokens": 256 }
  }

Notes on fields (why these):
- model_preferences: explicit ordered list used for deterministic fallback. Priority respects both policy and explicit list.
- max_cost_usd: safety valve for hosted customers to avoid runaway spend on long responses (approx unit cost estimate).
- kv_cache_hint: signal to runtime to check prefix cache and pin KV slot for this request scope. Not guaranteed but informs placement.
- partial_on_fallback: option for apps needing degraded responses instead of errors. Needs product approval.

Runtime config (server-side) - registry options:
- Each model entry in registry includes: model_id, variant_tags (q4, q5m, fp16), compatible_sequence_length, preferred_kernel_family, expected_token_cost_usd_per_1k
- Pool definitions: pool_id, capacity_gpus, latency_slo_ms, cost_tier (premium, standard, low), regions
- Routing policy engine will match: region -> pool cost/latency -> model variant -> fallback chain -> allocate batch slot

Example routing decision flow (rough):
1) Request arrives with prefer-latency + listed model preferences preferring us-west1
2) Check model registry for exact version. If available in premium pool in us-west1 -> schedule there.
3) If capacity constrained -> try same variant in other pool (same region) or next model preference in list.
4) If none available within max_cost_usd -> return 429 with structured payload explaining fallback attempt details

Telemetry / observability needs (minimal):
- Per-request: chosen_model, chosen_pool, fallback_attempts (list), decision_latency_ms, cost_estimate_usd, kv_cache_hit
- Dashboards: per-route P95 latency, per-model cost/unit, fallback rate by route

Open questions / TODOs:
- How expressive should route_config be for downstream SDKs? Do we expose full policy language or provide pre-sets?
- max_cost_usd semantics: should it apply per-token, per-request, or be advisory? (For now: advisory + best-effort enforcement)
- How to present fallback details to SDKs without leaking too much infra complexity? Suggest structured error codes plus a human-readable message.
- Security: pinned model versions for Private deployments must be enforced by private control plane; route_config should include a flag to disallow external model references in Private mode.

Prototype implementation notes (short):
- Step 1 (canary): implement model_preferences and simple fallback chain in serving runtime; add telemetry hooks.
- Step 2: add kv_cache_hint plumbing + per-route batching overrides.
- Step 3: wire route_config into Console UI -> small UX for policy presets (latency/cost/secure).

Sketch of textual diagram (placement):
[Client SDK] -> [API Gateway/Frontend] -> [Routing Engine (policy match + model registry)] -> [Pool Allocator] -> [Serving Runtime (GPU)]
                                |
                                v
                          [Cache Layer (KV/prefix)]

Sticky notes:
- Keep the initial API minimal; prefer pre-defined policies (latency/cost) rather than freeform policy DSL.
- Provide server-side defaults so users only set a couple fields for common cases.
- We need a short field mapping doc for SDKs: e.g., "latency_preset=low" maps to batching and pool selection rules.

Example quick todo (local):
- [ ] Write minimal router unit tests covering model preference fallback (RDW-1223).
- [ ] Add telemetry tags (chosen_model, fallback_count) to request proto.
- [ ] Draft Console UX copy for "policy presets" (Priya to iterate).

References / links:
- RFC: CON-8472 (should flesh out routing policy language)
- RDW-1223 Jira: router fallback tests
- PR: serving-runtime#459 contains partial routing plumbing work (look at pool selection code)

Notes-to-self: if we need to iterate quickly, keep API stable but add an experimental header X-RDWF-Routing that accepts a compact policy token (URL-safe) for internal usage only.

End of scratchpad.
